correctness.rationale: Exhaustive all-independent-subset enumeration constructs 6212 augmented faces (6211 nonempty), with face counts (1,20,160,660,1510,1924,1320,480,115,20,2). Staged toggling under the specified 20-label order yields 3103 disjoint augmented face pairs, exactly one critical four-face and five critical five-faces; the empty face is paired to one vertex. All 30380 directed cover incidences admit a complete 6212-vertex topological sort, certifying an acyclic matching. Integer signed elimination along the matching gives the five-by-one Morse degree vector (0,0,0,0,0), with two explicitly cancelling pairs of nonzero paths. Thus the ordinary CW complex has one zero-cell, one four-cell and five five-cells, all five-degree attachments null in \(\pi_4(S^4)\cong\mathbb Z\), proving \(S^4\vee\bigvee^5 S^5\). A second independent program builds isomorphic \(H(5,2)\), checks explicit isomorphism, f-polynomial and complete mod-two ranks. Both programs execute from the new embedded sources. No finite sampling is substituted for exhaustive verification, and no result for infinite families is claimed.

value.rationale: The twenty-vertex Desargues graph is a canonical cubic distance-transitive Levi graph of a natural 10-point/10-line configuration. Its independence complex has simplicial dimension nine but homotopy of a four-sphere and five five-spheres, an exact mixed-dimensional result not implied by triangle-free suspension, edge-ideal invariants, f-vector, or mod-two ranks. Integer attaching maps and free integral homology are fully determined. This exact homotopy type is a motivated natural invariant of a highly symmetric named graph and is reproducible by an exhaustive finite certificate; no general family extrapolation or downstream theorem is claimed.
